evidence_chain: Toast Q1 2026 operating scale: the company reported about 171,000 total locations, $51.3B GPV, ARR of about $2.2B, and 26% ARR growth year over year. Source: Toast Q1 2026 earnings release / SEC exhibit: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1650164/000165016426000113/tost-20260331xexhibit991.htm

Toast Q1 2026 profitability and guidepost: the company reported Q1 2026 free cash flow of $115M versus $69M in Q1 2025 and raised full-year 2026 guidance for recurring gross profit and adjusted EBITDA. Source: Toast Q1 2026 earnings release: https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260507253488/en/Toast-Announces-First-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results

Toast Q1 2026 prepared remarks disclosed that GPV per location was down 1% year over year, which matters because it separates location growth from per-location activity. Source: Toast Q1 2026 prepared remarks PDF: https://s28.q4cdn.com/141746709/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/TOST-1Q26-Prepared-Remarks.pdf

Industry demand driver: the National Restaurant Association’s 2026 State of the Restaurant Industry materials describe measured growth but continued pressure from uneven traffic, rising costs, cautious household spending, and margin challenges. Source: https://restaurant.org/research-and-media/research/research-reports/state-of-the-industry/

Industry cost pressure: the National Restaurant Association’s 2026 press release says total restaurant and foodservice sales are projected to reach $1.55T in 2026 and operators are forecast to add more than 100,000 jobs, while persistent cost pressure and cautious consumer spending remain challenges. Source: https://restaurant.org/research-and-media/media/press-releases/persistent-cost-increases-and-enduring-demand-will-shape-the-restaurant-industry-in-2026/

Margin pressure context: National Restaurant Association commentary noted restaurant labor costs remain well above historical averages, with salaries and wages including benefits historically around one-third of sales for full-service restaurants and around the high-20% range for limited-service restaurants. Source: https://restaurant.org/research-and-media/research/restaurant-economic-insights/analysis-commentary/restaurant-labor-costs-are-well-above-historical-averages/

Toast 2025 annual-report risk factors state that Toast depends on attracting new customers, retaining existing customers, and increasing customer use of its platform; pricing pressure and competition could reduce sales, margins, retention, and market acceptance. Source: Toast 2025 Form 10-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1650164/000165016426000097/toastinc10k2026v1-final.pdf

If operators cannot easily raise menu prices without hurting traffic, software that increases throughput, lowers waste, improves labor scheduling, and drives repeat visits becomes a more strategic budget item.

Toast’s strongest chokepoint claim is supported when subscription ARR, recurring gross profit, and module attach grow faster than pure location count, because that would show expansion within restaurant workflows rather than only new-location acquisition.

AI products such as Toast IQ / Toast IQ Grow could improve retention and ARPU if they demonstrably increase guest frequency, sales conversion, campaign ROI, or labor productivity; however, durable monetization and usage-based economics still need verification.
falsification_plan: Downgrade the thesis if net location additions slow materially for two or more quarters without offsetting ARPU, attach-rate, or margin improvement.

Downgrade the thesis if GPV growth remains positive but GPV per location, same-location GPV, or transaction activity deteriorates, suggesting weak restaurant throughput rather than true platform expansion.

Downgrade the thesis if subscription ARR or subscription gross profit decelerates faster than location growth, because that would weaken the claim that restaurants are attaching more software modules.
Downgrade the thesis if management commentary or filings show rising churn, weaker net revenue retention, longer implementation cycles, or lower customer satisfaction among SMB restaurants.
Downgrade the thesis if AI, marketing, payroll, inventory, loyalty, and ordering products fail to show measurable adoption, revenue contribution, or ROI evidence.

Downgrade the thesis if competitive pricing from Square, Clover, Oracle, NCR Voyix, PAR, Lightspeed, Shift4, or vertical software vendors forces lower take rates, higher incentives, or margin compression.
Downgrade the thesis if enterprise and international expansion require disproportionate sales, support, or R&D investment and dilute operating leverage.
Downgrade the thesis if restaurant-industry indicators show broad SMB closures, weakening traffic, or sharp reductions in technology budgets.
next_research_tasks: Pull Toast’s latest 10-Q and earnings-call transcript; extract ARR split, subscription ARR growth, fintech ARR growth, recurring gross profit, adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow, GPV per location, and any commentary on same-location GPV.

Search SEC filings and earnings-call Q&A for net revenue retention, gross churn, logo churn, cohort expansion, customer acquisition cost, sales productivity, and payback period. Mark any undisclosed metrics as evidence gaps.
Build a module-attach tracker for payroll, marketing, loyalty, inventory, online ordering, Toast Capital, Toast IQ, Toast IQ Grow, drive-thru, retail food-and-beverage, and international products.

Compare Toast against Square for Restaurants, Clover, Oracle MICROS, NCR Voyix/Aloha, PAR, Lightspeed, Shift4, Olo, and Restaurant365 on target customer, pricing, payment bundling, hardware lock-in, implementation complexity, and restaurant-specific workflow depth.

Map restaurant health indicators by segment: independent full-service, limited-service/QSR, bars, cafés, enterprise chains, hotel/retail foodservice, and international markets. Tie these to Toast exposure where disclosed.
Check whether GPV growth is volume-led or inflation-led by comparing Toast GPV per location with industry menu-price inflation, restaurant traffic, and same-store sales data.

Investigate AI product evidence: weekly active locations, pilot conversion rates, incremental revenue lift, pricing model, gross margin impact, and whether AI is bundled for retention or monetized as a paid module.

Create a quarterly falsification dashboard with thresholds for location net adds, GPV/location, subscription ARR growth, recurring gross profit growth, take rate, gross margin, adjusted EBITDA margin, free cash flow, and competitive win/loss commentary.
risks: Restaurant operator health could deteriorate. If independent restaurants face weaker traffic, higher failure rates, or reduced discretionary software spend, Toast may see slower net adds, higher churn, or lower expansion revenue.
GPV growth can be flattered by menu-price inflation. If transaction count, same-location sales, or GPV per location weaken, headline GPV growth may overstate platform health.

The operating-system thesis depends on customers adopting multiple modules beyond POS and payment processing. If payroll, marketing, loyalty, inventory, online ordering, and AI attach rates stall, Toast may remain closer to a payment/POS vendor than a full operating system.

Fintech revenue and gross profit depend on payment volume, take rate, processing costs, network fees, risk losses, and merchant pricing. Competitive pressure or regulatory/card-fee pressure could compress economics.

Square, Clover/Fiserv, Oracle MICROS, NCR Voyix/Aloha, PAR, Lightspeed, Shift4, Olo, Restaurant365, and enterprise in-house stacks may target the same restaurant workflows. Generalist payment platforms can compete on price; legacy enterprise systems can compete on installed base and customization.

Enterprise, drive-thru, retail food-and-beverage, and international expansion may require different product features, sales cycles, implementation support, and integrations than Toast’s core SMB restaurant base.

Even if the business performs well, public-market expectations may already price in strong ARR growth, margin expansion, AI monetization, and enterprise expansion. This report does not provide a buy/sell view or target price.

Key indicators such as net revenue retention, churn by cohort, module attach, AI monetization, and segment-level unit economics may not be fully disclosed, making the chokepoint thesis harder to verify from public data alone.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Theme map / 产业链位置: Restaurants → restaurant operators → front-of-house and back-of-house workflows → POS and order capture → payments and settlement → guest data, loyalty, marketing, online ordering, delivery integrations → labor, payroll, scheduling, inventory, menu and food-cost control → analytics/AI and capital products. Toast sits in the software-fintech operating layer between restaurants and their customers, staff, payment networks, banks, delivery channels, and suppliers. This is a horizontal workflow chokepoint because it touches transaction capture, payment monetization, restaurant data, customer retention, and operating decisions. Public-market mapping: Toast is the focused pure-play; adjacent/competitive mappings include Block/Square, Fiserv/Clover, Oracle MICROS, NCR Voyix/Aloha, PAR Technology, Lightspeed, Shift4, Olo, DoorDash/Uber Eats integrations, Restaurant365, and enterprise in-house systems.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: Toast 的核心卡点不是单一 POS 或收单，而是餐厅经营层的一体化系统：POS、支付、订阅软件、在线点餐、营销、忠诚度、排班/工资、库存、资金服务、AI 和客户触达。餐厅行业在 2026 年继续面对成本上升、客流不均、消费者谨慎、刷卡费和劳动力压力，这使得提升翻台、复购、劳效、菜单管理和运营可视化的工具更具刚需属性。Toast 2026 年一季度披露 ARR 同比增长 26% 至约 22 亿美元，地点数同比增长 22% 至约 17.1 万个，GPV 同比增长 22% 至 513 亿美元，并上调全年非 GAAP 订阅服务和金融科技解决方案毛利及调整后 EBITDA 指引。由此推论，Toast 可能成为餐厅数字化经营系统中更接近真实预算与工作流的瓶颈节点。待验证的关键是：增长是否来自真实模块增购和留存改善，而不只是地点扩张、餐饮通胀或支付流水放大。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Toast’s chokepoint is not a standalone POS terminal or merchant-acquiring function; it is the integrated restaurant operating layer spanning POS, payments, subscription software, online ordering, marketing, loyalty, labor/payroll, inventory, capital products, AI, and guest engagement. In 2026, restaurants continue to face cost inflation, uneven traffic, cautious consumers, swipe-fee pressure, and labor constraints, making tools that improve throughput, repeat visits, labor productivity, menu control, and operating visibility more mission-critical. Toast reported Q1 2026 ARR growth of 26% year over year to about $2.2B, locations growth of 22% to about 171,000, GPV growth of 22% to $51.3B, and raised full-year guidance for non-GAAP subscription-services and fintech-solutions gross profit and adjusted EBITDA. The inference is that Toast may be a high-purity public-market proxy for the restaurant operating-system bottleneck. The main unresolved question is whether growth is driven by durable module attach and retention, not merely location expansion, restaurant inflation, or larger payment volume.
deep_reports.title_cn: Toast：餐厅经营系统卡点的高纯度代理，但需验证增购、留存与支付经济性
deep_reports.title_en: Toast: A High-Purity Restaurant Operating-System Chokepoint, Pending Proof on Attach, Retention, and Payments Economics

evidence_chain: [Fact | Source: McDonald's Q1 2026 release] Global comparable sales increased 3.8% in Q1 2026, with solid growth across all major segments.

[Fact | Source: McDonald's Q1 2026 release] U.S. comparable sales increased 3.9% in Q1 2026; International Operated Markets increased 3.9%; International Developmental Licensed Markets increased 3.4%.

[Fact | Source: McDonald's Q1 2026 release / Morningstar mirror] U.S. comparable sales were primarily driven by positive check growth, which makes traffic contribution a key item to verify before upgrading the thesis.

[Fact | Source: McDonald's FY 2025 results / SEC 8-K exhibit] Across 70 loyalty markets, full-year systemwide sales to loyalty members increased 20% to nearly $37 billion, and 90-day active loyalty users rose 19% to nearly 210 million at year-end 2025.

[Fact | Source: McDonald's investor overview deck] Management has communicated ambitions to reach 250 million 90-day active loyalty members and $45 billion in annual loyalty systemwide sales by the end of 2027.

[Inference] Loyalty scale may improve personalized value offers, frequency, ordering convenience, and marketing ROI, but it must be tied to guest-count improvement rather than merely shifting existing customers into the app.

[Inference] McDonald's scale gives it more room than smaller restaurant operators to fund value menus, national promotions, media, procurement savings, and technology investments, but the cost burden may still pressure franchisees.

[Hypothesis] In a pressured consumer environment, the best restaurant equities to research may be those with scale-based value systems and repeat-traffic data advantages, not simply those with the fastest unit growth.
falsification_plan: Downgrade the thesis if U.S. comparable sales stay positive but management or filings show sustained negative guest counts.
Downgrade the thesis if positive comps are primarily check-driven for multiple quarters without evidence of traffic recovery.
Downgrade the thesis if value promotions require heavier corporate funding or create visible franchisee margin/cash-flow stress.
Downgrade the thesis if loyalty users and loyalty sales grow but frequency, visit count, or retention indicators do not improve.
Downgrade the thesis if international operated markets or developmental licensed markets decelerate materially versus U.S. performance.
Downgrade the thesis if menu innovation raises operational complexity without durable mix or traffic gains.
Downgrade the thesis if consumer surveys, app data, or third-party traffic data show McDonald's losing value perception to peers.
next_research_tasks: Pull the Q1 2026 Form 10-Q and earnings-call transcript to isolate traffic versus average-check contribution by segment, especially U.S.
Track 2026 quarterly disclosures for loyalty: 90-day active users, loyalty systemwide sales, digital mix, delivery mix, and evidence of frequency improvement.
Compare McDonald's U.S. traffic, average check, and value perception against Burger King, Wendy's, Taco Bell/Yum Brands, Starbucks, Chipotle, and quick-service industry traffic datasets.
Review franchisee economics indicators: restaurant margin dollars, rent/service fee burden, promotion funding, remodel capex, wage inflation, and franchisee commentary.
Map menu platforms by evidence quality: breakfast, beverages, chicken/McCrispy, Best Burger, large burger pilots, limited-time offers, and their repeat-purchase potential.

Check international markets separately: International Operated Markets versus International Developmental Licensed Markets, including China, Europe, Australia, Japan, and Latin America where disclosed.

Build a quarterly falsification dashboard with: U.S. traffic, U.S. average check, global comps, segment comps, loyalty users, loyalty sales, restaurant margins, value-promotion cadence, franchisee health, and unit development.
Compare valuation/pricing context without making a trade recommendation: current consensus expectations, multiple versus peers, and whether the market is already pricing a traffic recovery.
risks: [Risk | Traffic quality] Comparable sales can remain positive while guest counts decline if growth is driven mainly by price, mix, or average check.
[Risk | Franchisee economics] Value promotions may require rising corporate subsidy or may transfer margin pressure to franchisees, weakening system alignment.
[Risk | Consumer affordability backlash] If consumers continue to view fast food as too expensive, value campaigns may not fully repair traffic perception.
[Risk | Discount intensity] Competitive value wars across QSR could erode restaurant-level margins and make sales growth lower quality.
[Risk | Loyalty interpretation] Loyalty sales growth may reflect channel migration rather than incremental visits or improved retention.
[Risk | International exposure] International operated and developmental licensed markets may slow due to macro pressure, FX, local competition, geopolitical risk, or food-safety incidents.
[Risk | Input costs] Labor, commodities, occupancy, packaging, and delivery economics can pressure restaurant margins even when systemwide sales grow.
[Risk | Menu execution] Chicken, beverage, breakfast, burger upgrades, or new product platforms may fail to generate repeat visits or may complicate operations.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Demand layer: value-seeking QSR consumers, especially pressured lower-income and convenience-driven customers. System layer: global QSR operating model, franchise network, drive-thru, digital ordering, delivery, loyalty, and menu platform. Bottleneck layer: value-led traffic aggregation, promotion funding capacity, loyalty-driven retention, and franchisee unit economics. Supplier/input layer: food commodities, packaging, labor, real estate, technology vendors, delivery platforms, marketing/media, and franchise capital. Public-market mapping: MCD is the benchmark scaled QSR franchisor; related comparison nodes include other QSR franchisors/operators, coffee chains, fast-casual chains, delivery platforms, food distributors, and restaurant technology vendors.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 麦当劳的 Serenity 卡点不在单一门店，而在其能否用全球规模采购、品牌营销、数字会员、菜单工程、早餐/饮料创新和加盟体系，在消费者追求性价比、低收入客群承压的环境中守住客流与加盟商经济性。【事实露 2026 年一季度全球可比销售增长 3.8%，美国可比销售增长 3.9%，国际运营市场增长 3.9%，国际发展许可市场增长 3.4%；2025 年全年 70 个会员市场会员系统销售额接近 370 亿美元，90 日活跃会员接近 2.1 亿。【关键比销售增长主要来自真实客流、频次、会员复购和菜单组合改善，而不是单纯涨价或折扣换短期客单，则麦当劳可作为餐饮板块中“价值流量防御能力”的核心研究样本。
deep_reports.thesis_en: [Inference] McDonald's Serenity chokepoint is not the individual restaurant but the company’s ability to use global procurement scale, brand marketing, digital loyalty, menu engineering, breakfast/beverage innovation, and franchise economics to defend traffic in a value-seeking consumer environment. [Fact] McDonald's reported Q1 2026 global comparable sales growth of 3.8%, U.S. comparable sales growth of 3.9%, International Operated Markets growth of 3.9%, and International Developmental Licensed Markets growth of 3.4%. For full-year 2025, loyalty systemwide sales across 70 loyalty markets approached $37 billion, while 90-day active loyalty users approached 210 million. [Key judgment] The thesis is stronger if comparable-sales growth is supported by traffic, frequency, loyalty repeat behavior, and menu mix rather than mostly price/check increases or discount-funded short-term sales.
deep_reports.title_cn: 麦当劳：全球 QSR 价值流量系统的基准节点
deep_reports.title_en: McDonald's: Benchmark Node for the Global QSR Value-Traffic System

evidence_chain: Sysco reported fiscal Q3 2026 sales of $20.5 billion, up 4.7% year over year; gross profit rose 6.5% to $3.8 billion; gross margin expanded 31 basis points to 18.6%. Source: Sysco FY2026 Q3 earnings release, 2026-04-28, https://investors.sysco.com/annual-reports-and-sec-filings/news-releases/2026/04-28-2026-130535521

Sysco reported U.S. Foodservice case volume growth of 2.3% and local case volume growth of 3.3% in fiscal Q3 2026. Source: Sysco FY2026 Q3 earnings release, 2026-04-28, https://investors.sysco.com/annual-reports-and-sec-filings/news-releases/2026/04-28-2026-130535521

On 2026-03-30, Sysco and Jetro Restaurant Depot announced a definitive agreement under which Sysco would acquire Jetro Restaurant Depot; stated enterprise value was approximately $29.1 billion based on Sysco’s 2026-03-27 closing share price of $81.80. Source: Sysco acquisition release, https://investors.sysco.com/annual-reports-and-sec-filings/news-releases/2026/03-30-2026-113036743

【Fact stated Jetro Restaurant Depot had 166 large-format warehouse stores across 35 states, served more than 725,000 independent restaurants and foodservice operators, and generated approximately $16 billion of 2025 revenue. Source: Sysco acquisition release, https://investors.sysco.com/annual-reports-and-sec-filings/news-releases/2026/03-30-2026-113036743

The acquisition release states that Jetro Restaurant Depot would operate as a standalone business segment within Sysco and that closing is subject to customary conditions including regulatory approvals. Source: Sysco acquisition release, https://investors.sysco.com/annual-reports-and-sec-filings/news-releases/2026/03-30-2026-113036743
Q3 2026 margin expansion plus positive local case growth supports, but does not prove, the idea that Sysco has pricing, procurement or mix advantages in a pressured restaurant environment.

【HypJetro transaction could strengthen Sysco’s independent-restaurant reach by combining scheduled delivery, self-service warehouse replenishment and larger purchasing scale; this depends on regulatory approval, integration quality, and whether customer price/value improves rather than deteriorates.
falsification_plan: Downgrade the thesis if U.S. Foodservice total case growth or local case growth turns negative for multiple quarters.
Downgrade the thesis if gross margin expansion reverses while operating expenses continue to rise faster than volume, indicating weak operating leverage.
Downgrade the thesis if Sysco Brand/private-label penetration declines or management stops showing evidence that private-label and category mix support customer savings and gross profit per case.
Downgrade the thesis if independent restaurant customer retention weakens, sales headcount productivity falls, or local customer growth fails to continue.
Downgrade the thesis if the Jetro Restaurant Depot transaction is blocked, requires major divestitures, faces prolonged litigation, or closes with worse-than-expected financing/integration terms.
Downgrade the thesis if restaurant operators increasingly use club stores, regional distributors, direct sourcing or digital procurement platforms to bypass broadline distributors.
Downgrade the thesis if customer complaints and competitive responses indicate Sysco loses price credibility after acquiring a Cash & Carry competitor.
next_research_tasks: Pull Sysco FY2026 Q3 Form 10-Q and reconcile GAAP operating income, adjusted operating income, acquisition costs, interest expense and cash flow to test whether gross-margin improvement converts into durable free cash flow.
Track FY2026 Q4 and FY2027 guidance for U.S. Foodservice case growth, local case growth, gross profit per case, Sysco Brand penetration and operating expense growth.

Build a distributor comparison table: Sysco vs US Foods vs Performance Food Group vs Gordon Food Service vs regional distributors, covering revenue growth, case growth, gross margin, route density, leverage and independent restaurant exposure.
Research Jetro Restaurant Depot deal documents and SEC filings for financing mix, debt covenants, synergy assumptions, expected close timing and regulatory risk disclosures.
Monitor FTC/DOJ and state attorney general activity around the transaction, including second-request disclosures, litigation, divestiture requirements or settlement terms.

Collect independent restaurant operator evidence from trade publications, customer surveys and channel checks to test whether Jetro is viewed as a price-check alternative or a genuinely complementary replenishment channel.
Analyze category inflation/deflation trends in beef, poultry, dairy, seafood and produce to separate Sysco-specific margin power from commodity-cycle effects.

Estimate post-deal channel map: scheduled delivery, specialty distribution, Cash & Carry warehouse, private label, emergency fill-in purchases and digital ordering; identify where Sysco’s control is strongest and where customers can still bypass it.
risks: Antitrust and regulatory risk: the Jetro Restaurant Depot transaction is not closed as of 2026-06-07 and remains subject to regulatory approval. Blocking, divestitures, delays or behavioral remedies would weaken the multi-channel thesis.

Leverage and capital allocation risk: the proposed approximately $29.1 billion transaction is large relative to Sysco’s existing business and may increase debt, dilution, financing costs or integration burden.
Margin-quality risk: gross margin expansion may reflect temporary category inflation, pricing pass-through, mix, or timing rather than durable procurement advantage.
Volume risk: if restaurant traffic weakens, independent restaurants close, or local case growth slows, distribution density can work in reverse and pressure operating leverage.
Competitive risk: US Foods, Performance Food Group, Gordon Food Service, regional distributors, club stores and direct supplier relationships can pressure pricing and customer retention.

Customer perception risk: independent restaurant operators may view the Jetro acquisition as reducing a low-cost alternative to Sysco delivery, creating backlash or customer switching to regional distributors.
Execution risk: integrating a Cash & Carry culture with a broadline delivery model could damage Jetro’s value proposition if store-level pricing, product quality, autonomy or convenience deteriorate.
Cost inflation and deflation risk: food categories such as beef, poultry, dairy, seafood and produce can move sharply, affecting pass-through, customer budgets and gross profit per case.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Restaurant theme supply-chain map: 1) End demand: consumers dining out / food-away-from-home spend; 2) Operators: independent restaurants, chains, hotels, schools, healthcare and other foodservice customers; 3) Procurement node: broadline distributors, specialty distributors, Cash & Carry wholesalers, club stores and regional distributors; 4) Upstream supply: meat, seafood, dairy, produce, dry grocery, beverages, disposables and kitchen supplies; 5) Logistics infrastructure: cold chain, warehouses, route density, inventory management, last-mile delivery and customer support. Sysco sits at node 3 and node 5: a procurement aggregator and fulfillment network between fragmented restaurants and fragmented food suppliers. The proposed Jetro Restaurant Depot deal would extend Sysco from scheduled broadline delivery into Cash & Carry self-service wholesale.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 【推sco 的 Serenity 卡点不是单一食材，而是餐饮供应链的“密度型平台”：它通过采购规模、冷链与干货配送网络、品类管理、私有品牌、菜单成本支持、销售团队和客户信用/服务能力，帮助餐厅把碎片化采购转化为稳定补货。若餐厅行业持续面临食材成本、人工、客流波动和独立门店议价能力弱的问题，Sysco 这类 broadline distributor 可能成为餐厅利润率修复和生存优化的重要上游节点。拟收购 Jetro Restaurant Depot 若完成，将把传统配送网络与 Cash & Carry 仓储渠道结合，扩大对小型独立餐厅和临时补货场景的触达。
deep_reports.thesis_en: 【Inference chokepoint is not one food category; it is a density-based foodservice distribution platform. Its value comes from sourcing scale, cold-chain and dry-goods logistics, category management, private-label alternatives, menu-cost support, sales coverage, and restaurant service capabilities. If restaurants continue to face food-cost pressure, labor constraints, traffic volatility, and weak purchasing power, Sysco may become a critical upstream node for margin defense and procurement efficiency. If the Jetro Restaurant Depot acquisition closes, Sysco would combine broadline delivery with a Cash & Carry warehouse channel, expanding access to smaller independent restaurants and emergency replenishment use cases.
deep_reports.title_cn: Sysco：餐厅供应链中的广域补货、采购规模与独立餐厅服务卡点
deep_reports.title_en: Sysco: Broadline Foodservice Distribution as a Restaurant Supply-Chain Chokepoint

summary: Split Layer 5 deep reports generated one target at a time.
